A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: In the Netherlands, 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy was fully available (2001-2003 vs 2007-2009); the effect on the share of all lung cancer patients was not measured.
supported_en: A Netherlands Cancer Registry study (Annals of Oncology 2012) found 7% fewer elderly stage I patients untreated after stereotactic radiotherapy became available.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show the assumed 0.8-point rise in the share of all lung cancer patients treated with curative intent.
in_use_quote: Paikallisessa tai paikallisesti edenneessä taudissa, jos leikkaushoito ei ole mahdollista, voidaan antaa täsmäsädehoitoa tai yhtä aikaa säde- ja solunsalpaajahoitoa eli kemosädehoitoa.
in_use_summary_en: The OYS lung cancer care pathway (page dated 2025-09) says stereotactic radiotherapy can be given to local disease when surgery is not possible, and that the university hospital holds the multidisciplinary lung cancer meetings and gives the surgery and radiotherapy.
missing_en: No page shows a rule that every inoperable stage I patient, including those from Lapland, is referred to OYS for stereotactic radiotherapy.
summary_en: OYS's lung cancer care pathway says patients who cannot be operated can get stereotactic radiotherapy ("täsmäsädehoito"). It also says the university hospital runs the multidisciplinary lung cancer meetings and gives all lung cancer surgery and radiotherapy. No page says every frail stage I patient from Lapland must be referred. Dutch registry data (Annals of Oncology 2012) show 7% fewer untreated elderly stage I patients once the treatment was available, which supports the direction of the assumed effect but not its size.
unanswered_en: I found no Lapha page and no OYS page that sets a written rule to refer every inoperable stage I patient for stereotactic radiotherapy.
